content.caption:
Learn how to explain it properly in an interview. 

Interviewers want to understand your problem-solving, decisions and technical depth.

Structure your answers like this 👇

1️⃣ STAR — Tell your project story

Use when they ask: “Tell me about your project.”

S — Situation: Explain the problem, context or need.
T — Task: Define what you were responsible for.
A — Action: Focus on what YOU did  implementation, decisions, challenges and problem solving.
R — Result: Explain the outcome. Mention measurable impact or results when relevant.

⚠️ Keep Action as the biggest part.

2️⃣ PREP — Explain technical decisions

Use when they ask: “Why did you use X?”

P — Point: State your decision.
R — Reason: Explain the technical reasoning.
E — Evidence: Support it with requirements, constraints or results.
P — Point: Connect it back to the project requirement.

The important part is WHY, not just WHAT.

3️⃣ PROBLEM → APPROACH → TRADE-OFF

Use for architecture and technology questions.

Explain:

→ What problem were you solving?
→ What approaches did you consider?
→ What did you choose and why?
→ What limitations did it have?
→ What trade-offs did you accept?

This shows intentional decision-making.

4️⃣ ARCHITECTURE → FLOW → FAILURE

Use when the interviewer goes deeper technically.

Architecture: Major components and how they communicate.
Flow: What happens from user action to response/data change.
Failure: What happens when something goes wrong API failure, database failure, invalid input, timeout, duplicate requests, etc.

This tests your system understanding.

5️⃣ OWNERSHIP — Know what YOU did

For team projects, be ready to explain:

→ Your responsibilities
→ Your technical contributions
→ Decisions you made
→ Problems you solved
→ How your work connects with the rest of the system

Never claim work you can’t defend technically.

6️⃣ DEFEND YOUR DECISIONS

For every important technology or architecture choice, be ready for:

What? → Why? → Alternatives? → Trade-off? → What would you change now?

A strong project explanation isn’t a memorized speech.

knowledge.title: Interview Preparation: Structuring Your Answers and Defending Your Decisions
knowledge.summary: Learn how to structure your answers during an interview by using the STAR, PREP, PROBLEM → APPROACH → TRADE-OFF, ARCHITECTURE → FLOW → FAILURE, OWNERSHIP, and DEFEND YOUR DECISIONS frameworks. This will help you demonstrate your problem-solving skills, technical depth, and decision-making processes.
best_practices: Keep your answer focused on what you did, not just what you used.
mistakes_to_avoid: Never claim work you can’t defend technically.
Don't memorize a speech, but be able to explain your decisions and actions.
action_items: Learn about the PROBLEM → APPROACH → TRADE-OFF framework
Be ready to defend your decisions
